static_traits.name: Chen Da
static_traits.social_status: Has friends and family to confide in, but comfort has not yet eased Anxiety; recent Anxiety once strained relationships with colleagues
static_traits.medical_history: No major physical illness; previously no similar Anxiety problems; no history of psychotherapy/counseling
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, Good logic, high cooperation; frequently using negative predictions and catastrophic statements, repeatedly focusing on uncertainty (weather)

basic_info.main_problem: Feeling Anxiety about the upcoming Paris trip, firmly believing bad weather will ruin the itinerary, causing distress and Anticipation of negative experiences.
basic_info.core_demands: Anxiety has affected daily functioning and Work focus; hoping to ease travel-related Anxiety and recover focus and daily functioning.

core_beliefs: If the experience is not perfect enough, it is not worthwhile / equals failure

special_situations.event: Approaching the departure date and checking the week's weather forecast showing possible rain
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If the weather is not perfect, the trip will be ruined; I need to have everything certain before departure to be safe
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Excessively monitoring the weather, repeatedly refreshing apps and searching for information to try to gain a sense of control
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This time it will definitely keep raining; the trip will be completely ruined

special_situations.event: When planning the itinerary, thinking outdoor attractions may be affected by rain
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If plans are disrupted, time and money are wasted; all backup plans are inferior to the original
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Makes multiple backup plans but simultaneously belittles their value, lowering expectations to avoid disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As long as the weather is not good, this trip is not worthwhile

special_situations.event: Talking about worries with friends or family and receiving comfort and encouragement
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I need others' comfort yet remain Anxiety, it means the problem is serious and comfort is useless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly seeking reassurance, but quickly negating positive information
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: No matter how much they say it is useless; this time will surely be terrible

special_situations.event: Anxiety rising significantly when thinking about the trip alone (especially at night)
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Feeling bad now means the facts will be bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Through rehearsing the worst-case scenario to 'prepare psychologically', hoping to reduce disappointment
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I feel terrible, so this trip will surely be terrible

core_conflict.wish: Longing for a controllable, satisfying travel experience that can be fully enjoyed (longing for good things to truly happen and be one's own)
core_conflict.fear: Fearing disappointment and loss of control, worrying that uncontrollable external factors (weather) will take away joy and meaning
defense_goal: Avoids or reduces disappointment through advance monitoring and planning
Reducing the risk of hurt by lowering expectations

object_relations.self_representation: An anxious person feeling helpless about uncertainty, needing to ensure 'perfection' to feel at ease
object_relations.object_representation: Well-meaning but ineffective comforters / others who cannot truly solve problems

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor encourages challenging negative predictions with more balanced evidence and relaxing excessive control over the weather
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Feeling the other is asking one to 'settle', lowering standards, equivalent to accepting that imperfection will ruin the experience
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: First empathize with their fear of disappointment, slow the speech rate and use a gentle tone; then use Socratic questioning to help distinguish facts from predictions, possibility from necessity; provide a concrete both-hands preparation exercise, emphasizing that choice and control are in oneself.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When discussing backup plans (indoor activities, flexible itinerary) as a way to cope with uncertainty
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Seeing backup plans as 'all bad / settling', feeling that anything short of perfect weather equals failure
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Gently naming their 'all good / all bad' frame via mirroring, inviting examples of 'good and imperfect coexisting', encouraging small steps to experience 'good enough', reinforcing gray-area thinking.

manifestations: Worries bad weather will turn the trip into 'a waste of time and money'
Believing that if it is not perfect weather, the experience is 'not good enough' and not worthwhile
outcomes: Anxiety escalating with continued rumination on worst-case scenarios

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'.
manifestations: Internalizing 'only perfect weather counts as worthwhile' as a rigid standard, judging the travel experience with 'not good enough'
Even with backup plans, they are rated inferior to the original, making them hard to accept

positive_force: Previous personality relatively easygoing (usually rather relaxed)
Having a support network of friends and family
Has motivation to seek help and actively seeks counseling
Able to propose concrete attempts (checking forecasts less, considering backup plans)
Has a stable job and basic life structure
negative_force: A thinking pattern of catastrophizing and predicting the future
Perfectionistic expectations and black-and-white evaluation standards
Low tolerance of uncertainty and over-control (repeatedly checking weather)
Emotional reasoning and selective attention to negative information
Sleep, appetite and Impaired concentration triggered by Anxiety forming a negative cycle

target_behavior.behavior: Compulsively checking the weather forecast repeatedly
antecedent: When thinking of or discussing the upcoming Paris trip
Worrying outdoor activities will be affected when planning the itinerary
Seeing the weather app or related news
target_behavior.core_reason: Fearing disappointment and being unable to enjoy the trip, treating the catastrophic belief 'bad weather = ruined trip' as fact
target_behavior.function: Gaining a brief sense of control through information search, trying to reduce uncertainty and Anxiety
target_behavior.consequence: Slight short-term easing of unease but Anxiety maintained and intensified overall; Decreased work focus; disrupted sleep and appetite; Tense relationships with colleagues

target_behavior.behavior: Excessive travel-related Anxiety and worst-case rehearsal
antecedent: Repeatedly thinking about the itinerary when Being alone (especially at night)
Negative cues appear after checking the weather (such as 'it might rain')
After talking about the trip with others and receiving comfort, still repeatedly imagines the worst outcome
target_behavior.core_reason: Driven by fear of disappointment and the introjected rule 'not perfect = not worthwhile', tending to use worst-case Anticipation to prevent hurt
target_behavior.function: Mentally preparing by rehearsing worst cases for Self-protection (avoiding disappointment)
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent emotional distress, difficulty enjoying the preparation process; daily functioning impaired (sleep, appetite, and focus decline)
